statement_judged: On one pinned CPU of a RunPod Secure Cloud cpu5c pod (AMD EPYC 9575F; a shared cloud host, so the seconds are diagnostic), in this harness's implementation, 36 configurations (the 12 prime-order Weierstrass curves of the v5 study, group orders about 2^24, 2^28 and 2^32, seed 43, T = 1024/4096/16384) x 17 run keys x 3 interleaved repeats for each of two builds (std HashMap with SipHash; a fast multiplicative hasher, with identical counted operations), every target verified: the fastest of four multi-target index-calculus variants takes 0.70-0.88x (std) and 0.71-0.89x (fast) the solve-phase wall time of the fastest of ten multi-target rho runs at 2^24 and 0.79-0.95x and 0.74-0.94x at 2^28 (faster in 12 of 12 configurations at each size and build), and 1.05-1.18x (std; 12 of 12 configurations above 1) and 1.01-1.15x (fast; 11 of 12 above 1) at 2^32; the fast hasher speeds the fastest IC by 4-11% and the fastest rho by 0-15%; the IC takes 1.41-1.62x the time of a paired BSGS; the A/A control drifted (the first of three interleaved rounds about 3% slower), disclosed.
proposed_wording: On one pinned CPU of a RunPod Secure Cloud cpu5c pod (AMD EPYC 9575F; a shared cloud host, so the seconds are diagnostic), in this harness's implementation, 36 configurations (the 12 prime-order Weierstrass curves of the v5 study, group orders about 2^24, 2^28 and 2^32, seed 43, T = 1024/4096/16384) x 17 run keys x 3 interleaved repeats for each of two builds (std HashMap with SipHash; a fast multiplicative hasher, with identical counted operations), every target verified: per (size, T) cell, the median over its 4 configurations of the solve-phase wall time of the fastest of four multi-target index-calculus variants divided by that of the fastest of ten multi-target rho runs is 0.70-0.88 (std) and 0.71-0.89 (fast) at 2^24 and 0.79-0.95 and 0.74-0.94 at 2^28 (faster in all 3 cells and in 12 of 12 configurations at each size and build; single configurations 0.70-0.99), and 1.05-1.18 at 2^32 in the std build (slower in all 3 cells; 12 of 12 configurations above 1) and 1.01-1.15 in the fast build (slower in 2 cells, unranked at T = 1024; 11 of 12 configurations above 1). Each cell decision is a 4-of-4 sign rule (the bootstrap interval of a median of 4 equals their range). By cell median, the fast hasher cuts the solve time of the fastest IC by 4-11% and of the fastest rho by up to 15% (0.3% slower in the 2^32, T = 1024 cell), and the IC takes 1.41-1.62x the time of a paired BSGS; the A/A control drifted (the first of three interleaved rounds about 3% slower), disclosed.
